_comment: One end of a WireGuard tunnel: the fetchpoint. `wg-quick`'s field names, so an [Interface]/[Peer] stanza transcribes rather than translates, and a key pasted from one works in the other.

wireguard._listen_port: The port a peer dials and a NAT mapping belongs to. Required, never zero: an ephemeral port cannot be named to a peer or measured.
wireguard._address: The interface comes up holding this.
wireguard._private_key_env: `drt wg keygen` prints a pair. Read from the environment so the config carries the shape and never the value.
wireguard._stun: example: omits `stun` -- name two servers and the device measures its own mapping on listen_port before binding it, and reports the address a rendezvous should publish (doc/WireGuard.md §2)

peers._keepalive: What holds a punched mapping open.
